title: Personal pronouns: yo and tú
explanation: Spanish uses personal pronouns to show who is speaking or being addressed. In first-contact phrases, yo means I and tú means you. Spanish often omits pronouns because the verb form already shows the person, but beginners can use yo and tú to make meaning clear. Tú is informal singular you.
examples: Yo soy Ana. = I am Ana.
Tú eres Luis. = You are Luis.
Hola. Yo soy Ana. = Hello. I am Ana.

title: Ser in the present: soy and eres
explanation: Ser means to be. In first introductions, use soy for I am and eres for you are. The useful beginner pattern is Yo soy + name and Tú eres + name. Do not use soy with tú, and do not use eres with yo.
examples: Yo soy Ana. = I am Ana.
Tú eres Luis. = You are Luis.
Hola. Soy Ana. = Hello. I am Ana.

title: Saying your name: me llamo
explanation: Use me llamo plus a name to say your name. Use ¿cómo te llamas? to ask one person their name in a friendly informal situation. At A0, learn these as practical introduction patterns.
examples: Me llamo Ana. = My name is Ana.
Hola, me llamo Luis. = Hello, my name is Luis.
¿Cómo te llamas? = What is your name?

title: Saying origin: soy de
explanation: Use soy de plus a place to say where you are from. Use ¿de dónde eres? to ask one person where they are from. At A0, learn these as practical first-contact patterns.
examples: Soy de Madrid. = I am from Madrid.
Soy de México. = I am from Mexico.
¿De dónde eres? = Where are you from?
